taxonomy_basis.summary: Model species for vocal turn-taking and cooperative breeding; repertoire includes phee calls, trills, and alarm calls.

calls.acoustic_description: Long-distance, high-amplitude, tonal call, often produced as single or double phees with stable frequency contours.
calls.semantic_description: Long-distance contact, group cohesion, and coordination; central to antiphonal turn-taking.
calls.comments: Canonical marmoset call; extensively studied for vocal turn-taking and timing.

calls.acoustic_description: Short, rapidly modulated, tonal call of relatively low amplitude.
calls.semantic_description: Close-range contact and social cohesion; often exchanged during affiliative interactions.
calls.comments: One of the most frequent close-range calls in captive and wild settings.

calls.acoustic_description: Rapid series of short, high-pitched tonal notes.
calls.semantic_description: Arousal and excitement; often produced during movement or social activity.
calls.comments: Sometimes considered part of a graded continuum with trills.

calls.acoustic_description: Very short, high-frequency tonal call.
calls.semantic_description: Mild arousal, contact, or attention-getting at close range.
calls.comments: Often grouped with other short tonal calls in simplified repertoires.

calls.acoustic_description: Sharp, high-frequency call with abrupt onset.
calls.semantic_description: Alarm signaling, particularly for aerial predators.
calls.comments: Functionally referential alarm call documented in callitrichids.

calls.acoustic_description: Low-frequency, noisy call distinct from tsik.
calls.semantic_description: Alarm response, often associated with terrestrial threats.
calls.comments: Part of a predator-specific alarm system.

calls.acoustic_description: Broadband, high-amplitude scream.
calls.semantic_description: Distress and high-arousal social conflict.
calls.comments: Affective call common across primates.

calls.acoustic_description: High-pitched, repetitive distress vocalization.
calls.semantic_description: Care solicitation and distress signaling toward caregivers.
calls.comments: Strongly age-specific and central to cooperative breeding dynamics.

taxonomy_basis.summary: Known for extremely loud low-frequency calls enabled by enlarged hyoid; vocal repertoire well described at the genus level.

calls.acoustic_description: Extremely loud, low-frequency, long-duration roar produced using an enlarged hyoid; often occurs in extended bouts and choruses.
calls.semantic_description: Long-distance territorial advertisement, intergroup spacing, and mate defense.
calls.comments: Canonical howler monkey vocalization; function and morphology are exceptionally well documented.
calls.users: Primarily adult males; often chorused by multiple males

calls.acoustic_description: Short, abrupt, harsh call of intermediate amplitude compared to roars.
calls.semantic_description: Alarm, disturbance, or agitation contexts; sometimes used in intergroup encounters at closer range.
calls.comments: Common across Alouatta species; context-dependent usage.

calls.acoustic_description: Low-frequency, short-duration grunt; often produced in series.
calls.semantic_description: Close-range contact, coordination, and low-arousal social interactions.
calls.comments: Part of a graded close-call system; meanings inferred primarily from context.

calls.acoustic_description: High-amplitude, broadband scream, often given in bouts.
calls.semantic_description: Distress, aggression, or high-arousal social conflict.
calls.comments: Affective call type common across primates; well attested in howlers.
calls.users: All ages; especially juveniles and females

calls.acoustic_description: Low-frequency, harsh, growl-like vocalization, softer than full roars.
calls.semantic_description: Threat and aggressive display at intermediate distances.
calls.comments: Label varies across authors; often treated as a subcategory of threat calls.

calls.acoustic_description: High-pitched, tonal or noisy call emitted by infants.
calls.semantic_description: Care solicitation and distress signaling toward caregivers.
calls.comments: Ontogenetically restricted; not always included in adult repertoire summaries.

taxonomy_basis.summary: West African forest guenon famous for predator-specific alarm calling and structured alarm-call sequences. Adult males produce acoustically distinct alarm calls to crowned eagles vs leopards, and also use the same call types in ‘general disturbance’ contexts but with different sequencing rules (sequence length/structure conveys additional information). Diana monkey alarm calls are salient to heterospecific listeners (e.g., hornbills and other primates).

calls.acoustic_description: Loud alarm-call sequence dominated by exhalations with strong frequency transitions and characteristic inhalation units between calls (male loud-call form).
calls.semantic_description: Predator-specific alarm signaling terrestrial predators, especially leopards; also used in some sites as part of responses to leopard-like general disturbances, with meaning refined by sequence structure.
calls.comments: Canonical Diana-monkey predator alarm (male loud calls). Sequence composition (e.g., number of units/series) can add information beyond the call type.
calls.users: Primarily adult males (female repertoires include additional alarm/alert calls in some studies)

calls.acoustic_description: Loud alarm-call sequence with weaker/absent frequency transitions relative to leopard alarms; includes inhalation units between calls.
calls.semantic_description: Predator-specific alarm signaling crowned-hawk eagles (aerial predator); reliably discriminated by listeners.
calls.comments: Classic predator-specific alarm category in a forest guenon; heavily used in interspecific ‘semantic eavesdropping’ work.
calls.users: Primarily adult males (also produced by other group members depending on context/site)

calls.acoustic_description: Uses the same two basic male alarm-call types (leopard-type vs eagle-type acoustics) but typically arranged into longer or otherwise distinct sequences relative to predator-elicited sequences.
calls.semantic_description: Alarm/alert calling to non-predatory sudden disturbances (e.g., falling trees, fleeing ungulates, loud noises); sequence structure helps distinguish disturbance from predator contexts in some populations.
calls.comments: Included because multiple studies explicitly treat ‘general disturbance’ as a distinct eliciting context with consistent sequencing differences.

calls.acoustic_description: Low-amplitude close-range call (variously labeled as contact/close calls in guenon field coding).
calls.semantic_description: Close-range social contact and coordination within group (low arousal).
calls.comments: Diana monkey studies often focus on loud alarm calls; soft-call inventories are less uniformly enumerated across open sources, so this is included conservatively as a cross-taxon mapping element.

calls.acoustic_description: High-amplitude, broadband scream.
calls.semantic_description: Distress, submission, and escalation during aggressive interactions.
calls.comments: General affective call category included for cross-species completeness; not the primary focus of classic Diana alarm-call work.

calls.acoustic_description: High-pitched, repetitive distress vocalization.
calls.semantic_description: Care solicitation and distress signaling toward caregivers.
calls.comments: Ontogenetically restricted; included for schema consistency across primates.

taxonomy_basis.summary: Forest guenon best known for a small, male loud-call repertoire whose meanings depend strongly on call type and call sequences. Adult males produce two main alarm-call stems (pyow and hack) that can occur alone or in structured sequences (notably pyow–hack), with sequence composition conveying information about predator type and group movement rather than simple predator labels.

calls.acoustic_description: Loud, low-frequency alarm-call stem, acoustically distinct from hack; produced as single calls or repeated bouts.
calls.semantic_description: General alarm/alert call often given to leopards and to non-predatory disturbances; also used as a component in multi-call sequences.
calls.comments: Often treated as less predator-specific than hack; meaning depends strongly on sequential context.

calls.acoustic_description: Loud, sharp alarm-call stem, acoustically distinct from pyow.
calls.semantic_description: Predator-specific alarm call primarily given to crowned-hawk eagles (aerial predators).
calls.comments: Classic predator-specific alarm stem in forest guenons; rarely given outside aerial-danger contexts when isolated.

calls.acoustic_description: Structured sequence consisting of several pyows followed by several hacks (e.g., P–P–H–H).
calls.semantic_description: Group-movement initiation / travel signal rather than direct predator labeling; elicits coordinated group movement even in the absence of predators.
calls.comments: Canonical example of meaning emerging from call sequences rather than individual calls; frequently cited in discussions of compositionality.

calls.acoustic_description: Alarm calling dominated by pyow stems, sometimes in long or irregular sequences.
calls.semantic_description: Alert/alarm to non-predatory disturbances such as falling trees or intergroup encounters.
calls.comments: Often treated as context-dependent use of pyows rather than a distinct acoustic call type.

calls.acoustic_description: Low-amplitude close-range call produced during calm social interactions.
calls.semantic_description: Close-range social contact and coordination within the group.
calls.comments: Soft-call repertoire is less exhaustively enumerated than male loud calls; included for cross-taxon completeness.

calls.acoustic_description: High-amplitude, broadband scream.
calls.semantic_description: Distress and escalation during aggressive interactions.
calls.comments: General affective call category; not central to the classic alarm-call literature on this species.

calls.acoustic_description: High-pitched, repetitive distress vocalization.
calls.semantic_description: Care solicitation and distress signaling toward caregivers.
calls.comments: Ontogenetically restricted; included for schema consistency.

taxonomy_basis.summary: Forest guenon with a well-documented alarm-call system and social call repertoire. Red-tailed monkeys are central to studies of interspecific alarm-call eavesdropping and mixed-species associations. Their alarm calls distinguish major predator classes, and social contact calls are used extensively in cohesive group movement.

calls.acoustic_description: Short, sharp, high-amplitude call given singly or in brief series.
calls.semantic_description: Alarm signaling aerial predators, especially crowned-hawk eagles; elicits downward scanning and rapid movement into cover.
calls.comments: Functionally similar to eagle alarms in other forest guenons; reliably discriminated by listeners in mixed-species groups.

calls.acoustic_description: Lower-frequency, harsher alarm call than eagle alarms; often produced in short bouts.
calls.semantic_description: Alarm signaling terrestrial predators such as leopards; elicits climbing and arboreal escape responses.
calls.comments: Part of the classic guenon predator-specific alarm system.

calls.acoustic_description: Rapid series of harsh, staccato notes.
calls.semantic_description: Alarm signaling snakes and ground-based threats; often elicits approach, scanning, and mobbing.
calls.comments: Reported less consistently than eagle and leopard alarms but included in multiple field studies.

calls.acoustic_description: Low-frequency, resonant long-distance call produced singly or in pairs.
calls.semantic_description: Long-distance spacing, contact, and group coordination; often produced by males in non-urgent contexts.
calls.comments: Comparable to boom calls in other forest guenons; less emphasized than alarm calls in the literature.

calls.acoustic_description: Low-frequency, short-duration call, often produced in series at close range.
calls.semantic_description: Close-range social contact and coordination in low-arousal contexts.
calls.comments: Common affiliative call shared across cercopithecines.

calls.acoustic_description: High-amplitude, broadband scream, often in bouts.
calls.semantic_description: Distress and escalation during aggressive interactions.
calls.comments: Affective call common across guenons and macaques.

calls.acoustic_description: High-pitched repetitive distress vocalization.
calls.semantic_description: Care solicitation and distress signaling toward caregivers.
calls.comments: Ontogenetically restricted; central to mother–infant interactions.

taxonomy_basis.summary: Forest-dwelling guenon characterized by a relatively quiet social profile but a distinct male loud-call repertoire and predator-related alarm calls. De Brazza’s monkeys are often included in comparative guenon studies and mixed-species associations, though their vocal repertoire is less extensively catalogued than those of Diana or Campbell’s monkeys.

calls.acoustic_description: Low-frequency, resonant long-distance call, often produced singly or in short bouts by adult males.
calls.semantic_description: Long-distance spacing, group coordination, and advertisement of male presence.
calls.comments: Comparable to boom calls in other forest guenons, though produced less frequently.

calls.acoustic_description: Short, sharp alarm call, acoustically distinct from terrestrial alarms.
calls.semantic_description: Alarm signaling aerial predators such as crowned-hawk eagles.
calls.comments: Listeners in mixed-species groups respond appropriately to this call type.

calls.acoustic_description: Lower-frequency, harsher alarm call than eagle alarms.
calls.semantic_description: Alarm signaling terrestrial predators, especially leopards; elicits climbing and arboreal escape responses.
calls.comments: Part of the shared guenon predator-alarm system; fewer acoustic descriptions exist than for Diana monkeys.

calls.acoustic_description: Rapid series of harsh, staccato notes.
calls.semantic_description: Alarm signaling snakes or ground-based threats; often elicits approach and inspection.
calls.comments: Reported less consistently than eagle and leopard alarms.

calls.acoustic_description: Low-frequency, short-duration call, often produced in series at close range.
calls.semantic_description: Close-range social contact and coordination in low-arousal contexts.
calls.comments: Common affiliative call shared across cercopithecines.

calls.acoustic_description: High-amplitude, broadband scream.
calls.semantic_description: Distress and escalation during aggressive interactions.
calls.comments: Affective call typical of guenons and macaques.

calls.acoustic_description: High-pitched repetitive distress vocalization.
calls.semantic_description: Care solicitation and distress signaling toward caregivers.
calls.comments: Ontogenetically restricted; central to mother–infant interactions.

taxonomy_basis.summary: Forest-dwelling cercopithecine with a moderately described vocal repertoire including male loud calls, predator-related alarm calls, and close-range social calls. L’Hoest’s monkeys are often included in comparative guenon studies and mixed-species associations, but their vocal repertoire is less finely subdivided than that of Diana or Campbell’s monkeys.

calls.acoustic_description: Low-frequency, resonant long-distance call produced singly or in short bouts, primarily by adult males.
calls.semantic_description: Long-distance spacing, contact, and group coordination; may function as advertisement of male presence.
calls.comments: Comparable to boom calls in other forest guenons; acoustic descriptions are less detailed than for Diana or Blue monkeys.

calls.acoustic_description: Short, sharp alarm call acoustically distinct from terrestrial alarms.
calls.semantic_description: Alarm signaling aerial predators such as crowned-hawk eagles.
calls.comments: Listeners in mixed-species groups respond appropriately, indicating shared alarm semantics across guenons.

calls.acoustic_description: Lower-frequency, harsher alarm call than eagle alarms.
calls.semantic_description: Alarm signaling terrestrial predators such as leopards; elicits climbing and arboreal escape responses.
calls.comments: Part of the classic guenon predator-alarm system; fewer species-specific acoustic descriptions exist.

calls.acoustic_description: Rapid series of harsh, staccato notes.
calls.semantic_description: Alarm signaling snakes and ground-based threats; often elicits approach and inspection.
calls.comments: Reported less consistently than eagle and leopard alarms; included conservatively.

calls.acoustic_description: Low-frequency, short-duration call, often produced in series at close range.
calls.semantic_description: Close-range social contact and coordination in low-arousal contexts.
calls.comments: Common affiliative call shared across cercopithecines.

calls.acoustic_description: High-amplitude, broadband scream.
calls.semantic_description: Distress and escalation during aggressive interactions.
calls.comments: Affective call typical of guenons and macaques.

taxonomy_basis.summary: Open-habitat cercopithecine adapted to savanna and semi-arid environments. Patas monkeys rely heavily on visual vigilance and rapid terrestrial escape, and their vocal repertoire is comparatively simple. Alarm calls and loud calls are well documented, especially in predator contexts involving terrestrial and aerial threats.

calls.acoustic_description: Loud, harsh bark audible over long distances; often produced singly or in short bouts.
calls.semantic_description: Alarm and disturbance signal, particularly in response to predators or sudden environmental threats.
calls.comments: Primary alarm signal in patas monkeys; less acoustically differentiated than forest guenon alarm systems.

calls.acoustic_description: Low-frequency, far-carrying call produced by adult males, often from exposed positions.
calls.semantic_description: Long-distance spacing, advertisement of male presence, and group coordination.
calls.comments: Less stereotyped than forest-guenon boom calls; functionally similar in spacing and coordination.

calls.acoustic_description: Sharp, abrupt alarm call given singly or in short series.
calls.semantic_description: Alarm signaling aerial predators; elicits rapid scanning and fleeing into cover when available.
calls.comments: Aerial alarm responses documented, though acoustic differentiation is less pronounced than in forest guenons.

calls.acoustic_description: Low-frequency, short-duration call produced at close range, often in series.
calls.semantic_description: Close-range social contact and coordination in low-arousal contexts.
calls.comments: Common affiliative call shared across cercopithecines.

calls.acoustic_description: High-amplitude, broadband scream.
calls.semantic_description: Distress and escalation during aggressive interactions or predator attacks.
calls.comments: Affective call typical of Old World monkeys; not predator-specific.

calls.semantic_description: Care solicitation and distress signaling toward caregivers.
calls.comments: Ontogenetically restricted; central to mother–infant interactions.

taxonomy_basis.summary: Small-bodied forest cercopithecine with a socially tolerant structure and a relatively simple but active vocal repertoire. Talapoin monkeys produce frequent close-range contact calls and affective vocalizations; alarm calling is present but less semantically differentiated than in guenons such as vervets or Diana monkeys.

calls.acoustic_description: High-pitched, tonal or slightly modulated call produced frequently at close to medium range.
calls.semantic_description: Contact and group cohesion signal; maintains spatial cohesion during movement and foraging.
calls.comments: One of the most frequently produced talapoin calls; emitted by multiple group members during routine activity.

calls.acoustic_description: Short, high-frequency tonal call, often produced singly or in brief series.
calls.semantic_description: Short-range contact and attention-getting signal in low-arousal contexts.
calls.comments: Often treated as a subtype or variant of contact calls in some taxonomies.

calls.acoustic_description: Rapid, higher-amplitude version of contact chirps, sometimes repeated in short bursts.
calls.semantic_description: General alarm or alert to sudden disturbances or potential predators.
calls.comments: Alarm calling is present but less clearly predator-specific than in other cercopithecines.

calls.acoustic_description: High-amplitude, broadband scream, often produced in bouts.
calls.semantic_description: Distress and escalation during aggressive or high-arousal social interactions.
calls.comments: Affective call common across cercopithecines; used during chases and conflicts.

calls.acoustic_description: High-pitched, tonal, plaintive vocalization, often prolonged.
calls.semantic_description: Distress, protest, or appeasement in social interactions.
calls.comments: Often produced by juveniles and lower-ranking individuals.

calls.acoustic_description: Low-frequency, short-duration call produced at close range.
calls.semantic_description: Close-range social contact and coordination in low-arousal contexts.
calls.comments: Less prominent than contact twitters but present across contexts.

calls.acoustic_description: High-pitched repetitive distress vocalization.
calls.semantic_description: Care solicitation and distress signaling toward caregivers.
calls.comments: Ontogenetically restricted; frequent in infant handling and separation contexts.

species.completeness_warning: Talapoin vocal repertoires emphasize contact and affective calls; alarm semantics are less finely differentiated than in guenons. This entry reflects well-supported categories without speculative subdivision.

taxonomy_basis.summary: High-altitude grassland cercopithecine with one of the most complex and socially rich vocal repertoires among non-human primates. Geladas produce a large set of graded vocalizations used in close-range social interaction, affiliation, aggression, and sexual contexts. Vocal sequences and fine acoustic modulation play a central role in social bonding and negotiation.

calls.acoustic_description: Low-frequency, tonal, often prolonged vocalization; may occur singly or in sequences.
calls.semantic_description: Affiliative contact, reassurance, and social bonding in close-range interactions.
calls.comments: One of the most frequent gelada vocalizations; central to social cohesion.

calls.acoustic_description: Low-frequency, short-duration call, often produced in series.
calls.semantic_description: Close-range contact and coordination in low-arousal social contexts.
calls.comments: Functionally similar to grunts in other cercopithecines.

calls.acoustic_description: Rapidly frequency-modulated tonal call with oscillating pitch.
calls.semantic_description: Affiliative and appeasement signaling, often during grooming or approach.
calls.comments: Highly characteristic gelada call; often cited as analogous to human prosodic modulation.

calls.acoustic_description: Low-frequency vocalization accompanying exaggerated yawning display.
calls.semantic_description: Threat and dominance display in social tension contexts.
calls.comments: Often multimodal, combining vocal and visual threat elements.

calls.acoustic_description: High-amplitude, broadband scream, often in bouts.
calls.semantic_description: Distress and escalation during aggressive or high-arousal interactions.
calls.comments: Affective call common across cercopithecines.

calls.acoustic_description: Rhythmic, often tonal vocalization produced during copulation.
calls.semantic_description: Sexual context signal; may influence mate competition and social attention.
calls.comments: Sexual vocalizations are prominent in geladas relative to many other cercopithecines.

calls.acoustic_description: High-pitched repetitive distress vocalization.
calls.semantic_description: Care solicitation and distress signaling toward caregivers.
calls.comments: Ontogenetically restricted; central to mother–infant interaction.

calls.acoustic_description: Loud, abrupt bark-like call.
calls.semantic_description: Alarm or disturbance signaling, often to predators or sudden threats.
calls.comments: Alarm calls exist but are less semantically subdivided than in forest guenons.

species.completeness_warning: Gelada vocal repertoires are highly graded and continuous; this entry reflects well-supported call classes rather than fine-grained acoustic subtypes.

taxonomy_basis.summary: Forest guenon often found in polyspecific associations. Published sources emphasize male long-distance boom calls for spacing/coordination and a prominent loud alarm/warning role within mixed-species groups; a fine-grained, predator-specific inventory is less consistently enumerated in open sources than for Diana/Campbell’s monkeys.

calls.acoustic_description: Very low-frequency, resonant long-distance call (often produced in pairs or short bouts) emitted by adult males; carries well through dense forest.
calls.semantic_description: Long-distance contact/spacing and group coordination; reported to contribute to cohesion and movement control in polyspecific troops.
calls.comments: These sources treat boom-like loud calls as central to spacing/coordination roles in mixed-species associations; acoustic subtyping varies across field sites.

calls.acoustic_description: Loud, sharp, harsh call (often in bouts), acoustically distinct from low-frequency booms.
calls.semantic_description: High-arousal warning/alarm in disturbance and predator contexts; in polyspecific troops, adult males are reported to play a prominent role in aerial-danger warning relative to some associates.
calls.comments: Included conservatively as a widely reported loud warning call category; predator-specific partitioning is not exhaustively enumerated here for this species.
calls.users: Primarily adult males (others may alarm-call at lower amplitude)

calls.acoustic_description: Low-frequency, short-duration call, often produced in series at close range.
calls.semantic_description: Close-range contact and coordination in low-arousal contexts.
calls.comments: Common across cercopithecines; rarely enumerated in detail in older loud-call focused guenon papers.

calls.acoustic_description: High-amplitude, broadband scream, often in bouts.
calls.semantic_description: Distress and escalation during aggressive interactions.
calls.comments: Affective call category; included for cross-species alignment.

calls.acoustic_description: High-pitched repetitive distress vocalization.
calls.semantic_description: Care solicitation and distress signaling toward caregivers.
calls.comments: Ontogenetically restricted; typically not a focus of adult-male loud-call studies.

species.completeness_warning: Primary open-access sources for crowned monkey vocal behavior emphasize male boom/alarm roles in polyspecific troops; finer call-type inventories likely exist but are not exhaustively enumerated here.

taxonomy_basis.summary: Mona-group guenon. Published sources include descriptions of male long-distance boom calls and general guenon-like social/alarm vocal behavior; an openly accessible, exhaustive call-type list is less standardized than for Diana/Campbell’s/putty-nosed monkeys.

calls.acoustic_description: Low-frequency, resonant long-distance call produced by adult males; often given in bouts and audible over long distances.
calls.semantic_description: Long-distance spacing/contact and group coordination; may also function in territorial or intergroup contexts.
calls.comments: Boom calls are prominent in mona-group guenons and are specifically analyzed in mona monkeys in acoustic-variation work.

calls.acoustic_description: Loud, abrupt, harsh bark-like call.
calls.semantic_description: Alarm/disturbance signal in response to predators or sudden threats.
calls.comments: Included conservatively as a common guenon alarm-call class; predator-specific differentiation is not reliably enumerated in open sources for mona monkeys.

calls.acoustic_description: Low-frequency, short-duration call, often produced in series.
calls.semantic_description: Close-range contact and coordination in low-arousal contexts.
calls.comments: Common across cercopithecines; often under-described in older guenon loud-call sources.

calls.acoustic_description: Short, high-pitched tonal call, sometimes repeated.
calls.semantic_description: Short-range contact/attention-getting; can occur in mild alarm or arousal contexts in many cercopithecines.
calls.comments: Included for cross-species alignment; naming and partitioning vary across authors and sites.

calls.semantic_description: Care solicitation and distress signaling toward caregivers.

taxonomy_basis.summary: Large-bodied savanna-dwelling cercopithecine with a well-studied vocal repertoire dominated by graded social and affective calls. Chacma baboon vocal communication is central to social negotiation, affiliation, aggression, infant care, and group coordination, with extensive experimental and observational support.

calls.acoustic_description: Low-frequency, short-duration call, often produced singly or in series; acoustically graded.
calls.semantic_description: Affiliative contact and reassurance signal; commonly used during approaches and post-conflict interactions.
calls.comments: Classic example of functionally referential use modulated by social context; acoustic gradience is central.

calls.acoustic_description: Loud, abrupt, harsh call audible over long distances.
calls.semantic_description: Alarm, disturbance, or group-coordination signal in response to predators or sudden environmental changes.
calls.comments: Primary alarm call in chacma baboons; not finely predator-specific.

calls.acoustic_description: High-amplitude, broadband scream, often produced in bouts.
calls.semantic_description: Distress and escalation during aggressive interactions; recruits allies and signals submission or protest.
calls.comments: Highly graded; acoustic variation correlates with caller identity and social role.

calls.acoustic_description: Low-frequency, far-carrying call produced by adult males, often from exposed positions.
calls.semantic_description: Long-distance spacing, dominance advertisement, and group coordination.

calls.acoustic_description: Rhythmic vocalization produced during copulation, variable in amplitude and duration.
calls.semantic_description: Sexual context signal; may influence mate competition and social attention.
calls.comments: Well documented in baboons; function partly social rather than purely reflexive.

calls.acoustic_description: High-pitched repetitive distress vocalization.
calls.semantic_description: Care solicitation and distress signaling toward caregivers; elicits maternal and alloparental responses.
calls.comments: Central to infant survival; acoustically graded with urgency.

taxonomy_basis.summary: Widely distributed savanna–woodland baboon with a well-documented, graded vocal repertoire dominated by social and affective calls. Olive baboon vocalizations are extensively studied in the contexts of dominance negotiation, affiliation, aggression, infant care, and group coordination. Predator-specific semantics are weak compared to guenons; most calls are contextually graded.

calls.acoustic_description: Low-frequency, short-duration call, often produced singly or in series; acoustically graded.
calls.semantic_description: Affiliative contact and reassurance signal; commonly used during approaches, reconciliations, and benign social interactions.
calls.comments: Canonical baboon affiliative signal; acoustic variation reflects both caller identity and interaction context.

calls.acoustic_description: Loud, abrupt, harsh call audible over long distances.
calls.semantic_description: Alarm or disturbance signal in response to predators, sudden events, or intergroup encounters.
calls.comments: Primary alarm-type call in olive baboons; not strongly predator-specific.

calls.acoustic_description: High-amplitude, broadband scream, often produced in bouts.
calls.semantic_description: Distress, submission, and escalation during aggressive interactions; recruits allies.
calls.comments: Highly graded; acoustic structure correlates with aggression intensity and social relationships.

calls.acoustic_description: Low-frequency, harsh, growl-like vocalization.

calls.acoustic_description: Low-frequency, far-carrying call produced by adult males, often from elevated or exposed positions.
calls.semantic_description: Long-distance spacing, dominance advertisement, and group coordination.
calls.comments: Less stereotyped than forest-guenon booms; overlaps functionally with visual dominance displays.

calls.acoustic_description: Rhythmic vocalization produced during copulation, varying in amplitude and duration.
calls.semantic_description: Sexual context signal; may influence mate competition and social awareness.
calls.comments: Well documented in olive baboons; function interpreted as socially mediated rather than purely reflexive.

calls.acoustic_description: High-pitched repetitive distress vocalization.
calls.semantic_description: Care solicitation and distress signaling toward mothers and other group members.
calls.comments: Central to infant survival; reliably elicits maternal and alloparental responses.

species.completeness_warning: Olive baboon vocalizations form highly graded continua rather than sharply discrete call types; this entry reflects standard, widely cited call classes rather than fine-grained acoustic subcategories.

taxonomy_basis.summary: Small Australian oscine songbird and the canonical model system for vocal learning. Male zebra finches acquire song through imitation during a sensitive developmental period, producing a highly stereotyped adult song composed of ordered syllable sequences. The species combines learned song with a set of innate calls used for contact, cohesion, alarm, and parental care, making it central to studies of neural, developmental, and genetic mechanisms of learned vocal communication.

calls.acoustic_description: Highly stereotyped learned song consisting of a fixed sequence of syllables (motif), produced in bouts and directed toward a nearby female.
calls.semantic_description: Courtship and sexual advertisement; influences female mate choice.
calls.comments: Directed song is slower and less variable than undirected song; canonical focus of mate-choice experiments.

calls.acoustic_description: Learned song similar in structure to directed song but produced at higher tempo and with greater acoustic variability.
calls.semantic_description: Practice, song maintenance, and low-arousal social presence signaling.
calls.comments: Often interpreted as vocal practice or self-stimulation rather than direct communication.

calls.acoustic_description: Loud, tonal innate call with strong individual acoustic signatures.
calls.semantic_description: Long-distance contact and individual recognition between separated partners or group members.
calls.comments: Produced by both sexes; key signal for pair and group cohesion.

calls.acoustic_description: Short, soft contact call often produced in rapid series at close range.
calls.semantic_description: Close-range contact and social cohesion.
calls.comments: One of the most frequent calls in social flocks.

calls.acoustic_description: Rapid series of short broadband notes with rising urgency.
calls.semantic_description: Agitation, mild alarm, or social disturbance signaling.
calls.comments: Context-dependent; often produced during mild stress or social conflict.

calls.acoustic_description: High-amplitude, broadband call emitted during restraint or acute threat.
calls.semantic_description: Extreme distress; startle and escape contexts.
calls.comments: Innate call shared broadly across passerines.

calls.acoustic_description: High-pitched repetitive call produced by nestlings.
calls.semantic_description: Food solicitation directed at parents.
calls.comments: Classic model system for parent–offspring communication.

species.completeness_warning: Zebra finch song includes fine-grained syllable categories, acoustic micro-variants, and population-specific song dialects not enumerated here; this entry reflects standard call-type and song-category classifications used in behavioral and neurobiological research.

taxonomy_basis.summary: Neotropical leptodactylid frog and one of the most intensively studied models of acoustic communication and sexual selection. Male túngara frogs produce advertisement calls composed of a mandatory ‘whine’ and optional ‘chuck’ components. Call structure reflects a tradeoff between female mate choice and predation risk, making the species a canonical system for studying signal components, receiver bias, and signal evolution.

calls.acoustic_description: Frequency-modulated downward sweep (‘whine’) produced by calling males; can occur alone or as the core of more complex calls.
calls.semantic_description: Species recognition and mate attraction; minimal signal required to elicit female phonotaxis.
calls.comments: The whine alone is sufficient for female attraction but less attractive than complex calls.

calls.acoustic_description: Advertisement call consisting of a whine followed by one or more short broadband ‘chuck’ components.
calls.semantic_description: Enhanced mate attraction through additive signal components; increases attractiveness at the cost of higher predation risk.
calls.comments: Classic example of component-based signaling and receiver bias in sexual selection.

calls.acoustic_description: Shorter, harsher call produced during male–male interactions.
calls.semantic_description: Territorial or competitive signaling toward rival males.
calls.comments: Typically produced at close range during chorus interactions.

calls.acoustic_description: Loud, broadband scream emitted when seized by a predator.
calls.semantic_description: Extreme distress; startle or deterrence of predators.
calls.comments: Innate defensive vocalization common across anurans.

species.completeness_warning: The túngara frog repertoire is well characterized for mating and aggression contexts; rarer or developmental vocalizations are not exhaustively treated here.

taxonomy_basis.summary: North American hylid frog widely used as a baseline model for anuran acoustic communication. Male green tree frogs produce stereotyped advertisement calls for mate attraction, along with distinct aggressive, release, and distress calls. The repertoire is small, innate, and strongly context-bound, making this species a useful contrast to both vocal-learning birds and component-based frog systems such as the túngara frog.

calls.acoustic_description: Loud, repetitive nasal call consisting of a series of pulsed notes, produced rhythmically by calling males.
calls.semantic_description: Mate attraction and species recognition during the breeding season.
calls.comments: Primary call used in choruses; highly stereotyped across individuals.

calls.acoustic_description: Shorter, harsher call with reduced pulse structure compared to the advertisement call.
calls.semantic_description: Male–male aggression and spacing within breeding choruses.
calls.comments: Typically produced during close-range competitive interactions.

calls.acoustic_description: Brief pulsed call emitted when clasped during inappropriate amplexus.
calls.semantic_description: Signals mis-clasping and induces release by the other individual.
calls.comments: Common across anurans; produced by both sexes.

calls.acoustic_description: Loud, broadband scream produced when seized by a predator.
calls.semantic_description: Extreme distress; startle or deterrence of predators.
calls.comments: Innate defensive vocalization conserved across frogs.

calls.acoustic_description: Increased calling rate and overlap among males under humid or rainy conditions.
calls.semantic_description: Breeding coordination and chorus synchronization under favorable environmental conditions.
calls.comments: Often treated as a contextual modulation rather than a discrete call type.

species.completeness_warning: The green tree frog repertoire is small and well characterized; rare developmental or abnormal vocalizations are not included.

species.species_name: Poison dart frogs (Oophaga spp. / Dendrobates spp.)

taxonomy_basis.summary: Neotropical dendrobatid frogs known for conspicuous coloration and well-studied acoustic signaling associated with territorial defense, mate attraction, and parental care. Unlike many anurans, poison dart frogs often show individual recognition, graded territorial signaling, and sex-specific roles in calling. Their vocal systems are innate but exhibit fine-scale contextual modulation.

calls.acoustic_description: Short, stereotyped tonal or pulsed call repeated at regular intervals by males.
calls.semantic_description: Mate attraction and species recognition; also advertises male presence to rivals.
calls.comments: Primary call type used during breeding periods; structure varies across species.

calls.acoustic_description: Modified advertisement call with changes in rate, duration, or amplitude, often produced during interactions with neighboring males.
calls.semantic_description: Territorial defense and spacing between rival males.
calls.comments: Playback experiments show graded escalation and individual-specific responses.

calls.acoustic_description: Softer, short-range call produced during close male–female interactions.
calls.semantic_description: Courtship coordination and pair formation.
calls.comments: Low-amplitude and often omitted from coarse repertoire surveys.

calls.acoustic_description: Harsh, rapid call produced during escalated male–male confrontations.
calls.semantic_description: High-intensity aggression and territorial escalation.
calls.comments: Typically occurs at very close range and may accompany physical displays.

calls.acoustic_description: Loud, broadband scream emitted when seized by a predator.
calls.semantic_description: Extreme distress; startle or deterrence of predators.
calls.comments: Innate defensive vocalization shared with many anuran species.

species.completeness_warning: Dendrobatid vocal repertoires vary across genera and species; this entry reflects a conservative synthesis of well-studied call categories rather than an exhaustive species-level inventory.
